newsitem.title: USA: Macedonia sets debt deal with Chase, banks.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia sets debt deal with Chase, banks.

text.p: The Republic of Macedonia settled with its commercial bank creditors on an agreement under which Macedonia will exchange new bonds for its share of the debt of former Yugoslavia, Macedonia and Chase Manhattan Corp said Wednesday.

Under the agreement, Macedonia will issue bonds in exchange for its 5.4 percent of the $4.3 billion debt of the former republics of Yugoslavia. Macedonia said it will also issue fresh bonds in an amount equal to 3.65 percent of the past-due-interest and interest-on-interest of the old debt.
The new bonds will be amortized in stepped-up payments over 11 years following a four year grace period.

After the grace period, the interest rate will be LIBOR plus 13/16 percent annually. During the grace period, Macedonia will pay 3.5 percent for the first two years, and 3.75 percent for the second two years, with the difference between these fixed cash interest payments and the LIBOR plus 13/16 being capitalized.
The exchange is expected to take place before March 31, 1997, the release said.
In a 1988 accord, the former Yugoslav republics each assumed a defined portion of foreign commercial bank debt under an international formula.
Rescheduling accords were seen as essential for the republics to regain access to international capital markets.
Chase Manhattan Bank acted as chair of the international coordinating committee that represented commercial bank creditors.
